aggressive_definition: High-grade incident prostate cancer, defined as Gleason grade 7-10
aggressive_definition_excerpt: high-grade disease (Gleason grade, 7-10; overall Q5 HR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.13-2.24; P-trend = 0.001; among men receiving selenomethionine, Q5 HR, 2.12; 95% CI, 1.32-3.40; P-trend = 0.0002).
study_design: Prospective stratified case-cohort analysis derived from the SELECT randomized trial
reason: The abstract analyzes both overall incident prostate cancer and high-grade incident prostate cancer defined by Gleason grade 7-10. It gives the subcohort and case counts but not the unique combined analytic sample size in the abstract.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Men with higher α-tocopherol concentrations seemed to have risk similar to that of men with lower concentrations [overall HR for fifth (Q5) vs. first quintile (Q1), 1.21; 95 % confidence interval (CI), 0.88-1.66; P-trend = 0.24; in the trial placebo arm, Q5 HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.44-1.62; P-trend = 0.66].
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate is explicitly labeled overall and therefore represents general incident prostate cancer, not high-grade disease.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Men with higher α-tocopherol concentrations seemed to have risk similar to that of men with lower concentrations [overall HR for fifth (Q5) vs. first quintile (Q1), 1.21; 95 % confidence interval (CI), 0.88-1.66; P-trend = 0.24; in the trial placebo arm, Q5 HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.44-1.62; P-trend = 0.66].
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate is for overall incident prostate cancer. The paper's separate high-grade analysis does not make this overall estimate aggressive.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Incidence of prostate cancer as a function of plasma α-tocopherol, γ-tocopherol, and supplementation with α-tocopherol or selenomethionine was estimated by the hazard ratio (HR).
estimate_classifications.reason: The row concerns a selenomethionine-versus-placebo estimate for incident prostate cancer overall. The abstract supports the general endpoint, while the row's specific numerical contrast comes from existing full-text evidence.

additional_estimates.comparison: Fifth (Q5) versus first quintile (Q1) of baseline plasma α-tocopherol
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: A positive plasma α-tocopherol-prostate cancer association also seemed limited to high-grade disease (Gleason grade, 7-10; overall Q5 HR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.13-2.24; P-trend = 0.001; among men receiving selenomethionine, Q5 HR, 2.12; 95% CI, 1.32-3.40; P-trend = 0.0002).
additional_estimates.endpoint_definition: High-grade incident prostate cancer, defined as Gleason grade 7-10

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
